modules.name: Vista audit, node contract and frame rule
modules.design_question: Which Vista parts become the View-and-Warn node, what typed ports does it expose, and in which frame does each calculation run?
modules.method: Vista v09.16 is one WebGL2 page: explorer.js (218 KB, 161 functions, one global state), report.js, pdf.js, six self-test scripts. KEEP: polygon-clip kernels, result precedence and no-compliance wording guards, fixtures F1-F3, hash state, PDF writer, cone-fit camera rule. REFACTOR: split explorer.js into assets, picking, camera and ui modules; typed functions replace the global state and /api/check shim; checks run in a Worker; self-tests headless. REPLACE: the 38.7 MB triangle context, estimated origins, the flat ceiling as main test, per-part bounding boxes, Form Studio's duplicate cone copy, and the Vista equirectangular frame (0.20% short east-west, 0.58% north-south). FRAME RULE: containment and clipping run only in the EPSG:3157 grid (cones, site and design projected; edges grid-straight, as the City layer stores them); distances, azimuths and Dx come only from GeographicLib on GRS80, never mixed with grid bearings; z stays orthometric in the datum of the limit, never an ENU up axis. City layers get no datum shift (checked to 0.0002 m); OSM and GNSS inputs are flagged. The Site port tests polygons only. Every output carries units, CRS, datum, dataset versions and an estimate flag. Datum UNKNOWN: viewing works, numbers are blocked. Add MIT or Apache-2.0 licences and an ODbL and OGL-Vancouver NOTICE.
inputs: ConeSet: per view id, City-service apex and Lv with quality level, plan polygon, limit parameters (slope s, tier, reference, status), amendment years, service edit stamps and geometry hash
TerrainSampler: z(x,y), vertical datum, sigma, source tile ids
ContextTiles: LOD1 buildings with height source, epoch and datums
DesignMassing: placed triangle meshes, layers, units, horizontal and vertical datum (vertical may be UNKNOWN)

SiteSpec: City parcel polygon, or a hypothetical block in local coordinates with placed or unplaced status

HeadroomMap: two surfaces (clear-below, surely-above) minus grade, with a state code
ViewRender: existing and proposed images with overlays
SkylineProfile: elevation angle against azimuth
PdfReport
Provenance: dataset versions, hashes, assumptions

modules.name: Protected-viewpoint camera rig
modules.design_question: How do we render the design from each protected origin with correct position, eye height and a field of view matched to the cone?
modules.method: Origin: the City ViewCone service gives the apex (EPSG:26910, equal to the open-data apex) and Lv (VIEWPOINT_ELEVATION_M): quality Q1. Eye z = City Lv when present (Lv sits 1.40-1.87 m above the HRDEM ground at 12 of 17 origins, so it already looks like eye level: add nothing), else ground z + 1.6 m, editable. LiDAR-2022 checks Lv (0.081 m at 95%, land cover not stated); piers, bridges and seawalls (E, G1, G2, K, 10) differ by 2.3-13.8 m and keep Lv. Heading = bisector of the boundary azimuths. Presets: cone-fit (Vista rule hfov = clamp(1.5 x spread + 8, 24, 100)); standard 39.6 deg human view; cylindrical strip when hfov exceeds 60 deg (only view 27.2); QE-brief, the Brief p.30 skyline view from the 3.2.x origin, calibrated to the supplied photo (never bundled). Depth: reversed-Z when EXT_clip_control exists, else logarithmic depth; store the path on the camera record; near 1-2 m, far at least 60 km. Haze: none for evidence captures; the Vista context fog is removed. Render and profile share one apparent-drop function (M05). The limit overlay is a horizontal line at elevation atan(s) from the eye. Subject-visible test checks silhouette-to-sky contrast, not depth alone.

TerrainSampler ground z at the origin (LiDAR DTM, DSM on structures)

modules.name: Rooftop and surrounding-building viewpoints
modules.design_question: How do we offer trustworthy views from nearby roofs and rank which ones matter?
modules.method: Vista picks the highest modelled roof triangle (normal Z share at least 0.35), prefers high, broad, central surfaces, lists up to six buildings within 600 m and sets the eye 1.6 m above the roof; its roof heights are OSM-derived and unverified. Upgrade after 30 Nov: (1) roof z from LiDAR-2022 first returns and building-class points per footprint (CGVD28; the portal figure of 0.081 m at 95% does not name roofs, so measure it), shown beside OSM height plus LiDAR ground, footprints-2009 topelev_m (2009, stale) and, outside the City, HRDEM DSM where it has data (CGVD2013, about +0.15 m preliminary shift); spread = max minus min; (2) flag appurtenances, which OSM height excludes; (3) rank candidates by elevation angle to the design top, distance, unobstructed ray (BVH) and whether the roof lies inside any cone; (4) a grid index replaces whole-city scans; (5) access stays unknown unless a public viewing roof is listed; (6) never imply a rooftop is an official viewpoint. Output RooftopViewpoint with source, roof z plus or minus spread and building id. Reuse the Vista rooftop self-test (stable building ids restored from the URL hash).

modules.name: Cone limit estimate, states and exceedance warning
modules.design_question: How do we estimate each cone limit at any point and warn which cone, by how many metres, where, citing the clause and saying it is an estimate?
modules.method: The Guidelines (s.2, p.3) define a cone as two vertical boundaries plus a lower boundary setting the maximum geodetic height. Polygons give plan extent only. City sheet points fit a plane through the origin, L = Lv + s D (A: s 0.05889; 3.2.3: 0.000404): a constant elevation angle, a horizontal line in the origin view. Flat L is a what-if. Lv is the City service value. Tiers: T0 what-if; T1a slope fitted from 2+ published site-vertex limits; T1b slope (Lr - Lv)/Dr from a Council-stated or LiDAR-2022 roof reference (roof route untested); T2 City-confirmed. Plan test: polygon clip in the EPSG:3157 grid with buffer b, on site polygons only. Height: e = z_top - L, z orthometric. U95 = kc u_c, kc = 2 (GUM 6.3.3); fitted limits use Student t. States: outside; near edge; limit unknown; datum unknown; clear (e < -U95); within uncertainty (|e| <= U95); above (e > U95). Overall clear needs every covering cone determinate. Cards rank cones by state, then e. HeadroomMap holds min(L - U95) and min(L + U95), minus grade; the band between is within uncertainty. The UI says above estimated limit, never violation: clause 3.1.1 is guidance.

parameters.name: L(P)
parameters.relationship: Default L = Lv + s D, D the grid distance from the origin along the cone axis (radial fits A worse, 0.037 against 0.012 m): constant elevation angle atan(s). Flat L = L0 (s = 0) is T0 only.

parameters.name: Hx
parameters.relationship: L(P) - Lbx: maximum height above site grade; LiDAR grade error passes 1:1 into Hx.

parameters.name: e
parameters.relationship: z_top(P) - L(P) at the worst clipped vertex; positive means above the estimated limit; z orthometric in the datum of the limit, never the ENU up axis.

parameters.name: u_c
parameters.relationship: sqrt(u_L^2 + u_grade^2 + u_datum^2); planar u_L^2 = u_Lv^2 + (D u_s)^2; u_grade 0.04 m (0.081 m at 95% over 1.96); u_datum 0 for CGVD28, 0.15 m for CGVD2013; Lv rounding 0.1 m (QE), 1 m (10, G).

parameters.name: U95
parameters.relationship: U95 = kc u_c; kc = 2 (GUM 6.3.3: about 95% if near-normal with many dof); fitted limits use Student t with n - p dof (12.71, 4.30 for 1, 2 dof; GUM Table G.2). Print (95%) beside every +/-.

parameters.name: u_Lr (tier T1b)
parameters.relationship: LiDAR roof as Lr: roof-definition ambiguity (parapet, penthouse, pitched facets), 3 m standard-uncertainty placeholder, scaled by D/Dr into the plane. Council-stated Lr: 0.3 m team placeholder. Replace by the measured T1b residual.

parameters.name: U (fitted limit)
parameters.relationship: var L(D) = sigma^2 (1/n + (D - xbar)^2 / Sxx) from the least-squares fit; t with n - p dof (p = 1 for a plane through Lv). Leave-one-out residuals (A 0.017 m, 3.2.3 0.004 m) are in-sample only.

parameters.name: state thresholds
parameters.relationship: clear if e < -U95; within uncertainty if |e| <= U95; above if e > U95; ties go to the more cautious state. Example: e = -3.1 m with T1b U95 = 6 m is within uncertainty, not clear.

parameters.name: unknown states
parameters.relationship: Limit unknown: inside plan or buffer, no L at any tier; amber, plan overlap only, prompt to enter or confirm a limit. Datum unknown: relative heights only, exceedance numbers blocked. Neither may ever display as clear.

parameters.name: plan_buffer
parameters.relationship: b = 2 x sqrt(sigma_origin^2 + sigma_hdatum^2 + sigma_footprint^2); defaults 5, 2 and 1 m give 10.95 m; EPSG lists 1.0 m (default) or 2.0 m accuracy for NAD83(CSRS) to WGS 84.

parameters.name: band rule
parameters.relationship: Inside the buffer but outside the polygon, the nearest cone L applies and the card shows the edge distance in metres; near edge with no estimated exceedance is a quiet amber chip, not a full warning.

parameters.name: headroom surfaces
parameters.relationship: Per 25 m cell: clear-below = min_i(L_i - U95_i) - grade; surely-above = min_i(L_i + U95_i) - grade; the band is hatched within uncertainty. A covering cone without a limit makes the cell limit unknown.

parameters.name: status gate

modules.name: Skyline comparison and PDF report
modules.design_question: How do we show what the design changes in the existing view and export it as evidence?
modules.method: Render Existing and Proposed from one camera with a wipe slider. Skyline profile: for each azimuth (step 0.1 deg; 0.05 deg for cones narrower than 5 deg) across the cone plus 2 deg each side, march outward over a heightfield and keep the maximum elevation angle; or read the top pixel of each image column. Apply the apparent drop (1-k) d^2/(2R), k = 0.13, to the profile and the render with one function, never to the City limit numbers. Rays = (spread + 4 deg)/step: 56 or 112 for the 1.61 deg cone, 570 or 1,140 for the 53 deg cone. Outputs: three angle arrays, skyline area added (deg^2), share of cone width where the design rises above the existing skyline, margin to the estimated limit line. Keep the Vista report engine; add a vector profile chart, exceedance table with +/-U95, datum line, tier, estimate stamp and a provenance appendix with dataset dates and hashes. Print the context epoch (LiDAR 2022-09, OSM access date, studio-model date) on each image, with a toggle between existing as of 2022 and existing plus pipeline masses. Add alt text, non-colour cues (WCAG 1.4.1) and a live status region (WCAG 4.1.3).

modules.name: Design ingest and georeferencing
modules.design_question: How do .3dm, OBJ and IFC models become a placed, mesh-level DesignMassing with an explicit datum?
modules.method: Vista reads .3dm in the browser with rhino3dm (WebAssembly, MIT): meshes, extrusions and brep render meshes, a unit table (mm to yards), caps of 80 MB and 2 M triangles; OBJ is parsed locally; placement puts the model bounding-box base on the terrain at the site; the cone check uses one bounding box per part, which can overestimate. New contract DesignMassing {parts[id, layer, positions Float32, indices Uint32], units, source SHA-256, placement{anchor lat/lon, rotation, base z, datum}}. Placement modes: on site (as Vista), base z from the LiDAR-2022 DTM with its sigma shown; as-modelled coordinates with declared EPSG (EPSG:3157 for Vancouver) and vertical datum; hypothetical block loaded from the user own competition download, unplaced until dropped on the map. Models in true-north axes are rotated by grid convergence (about 0.1 deg: 0.27 m across a 144.8 m block). Vertical datum may be UNKNOWN: view only, exceedance numbers blocked. Layers named mechanical, antenna or mast are flagged appurtenances (clause 3.1.1 includes them). IFC through web-ifc; breps without render meshes are reported, never dropped. Test: the triangle check equals the box check on boxes and is lower on a stepped tower. Nothing is uploaded.

modules.name: Student-laptop performance and storage budget
modules.design_question: What size and compute budget keeps the node usable on a student laptop and on GitHub Pages?
modules.method: Baseline: the Vista pack is 38.7 MB with 1.09 M building triangles; queries scan triangles linearly. At the GitHub Pages soft 100 GB per month, 38.7 MB per load allows about 2,600 loads; 3 MB about 33,000. Targets: 5 MB to first interaction, 20 MB total, 30 fps on integrated graphics, 500 MB tab memory. Offline pipeline (py -3.13 with laspy and numpy; python on PATH is 3.9): scripted GET of City LAS zips returns HTTP 403, so a person downloads the 14 MVP tiles in a browser; the script reads each in chunks, grids ground and roof maxima, writes int16 decimetre heightfields (1 m within 50 m of each origin, 5 m downtown) and deletes the LAS. Worst case 14 x 2.74 GB. The City 2013 DEM (1.91 GB) is the one-file fallback. Backdrop: HRDEM has no data at the five peaks, so MRDEM-30 at native 30 m with max-preserving resampling; extent = cone sectors plus 2 deg to the first horizon ridge. Later: LOD1 int16 rings (about 50 B per building) in 500 m tiles, BVH, Workers, service-worker cache, 2D fallback. Verify on three laptop classes (thin-and-light and Apple M-class included) with a fixed benchmark scene.

modules.design_question: What can GPT-6 Astra and Claude do for this node, and where must survey data and people decide?
modules.method: Allowed, always with a human or deterministic check: code, tests and refactoring of Vista modules; data-cleaning and LiDAR-tile scripts; structuring text already extracted from PDFs into candidate rows (RTS 16338 Table 2, rezoning booklets); reading figures; review of one model work by the other; UI copy written from an ExceedanceReport JSON; fixture generation. Release gate (CI): guidelines.lock.json holds the SHA-256 of the team 2026 Guidelines copy (Vista records access on 2026-09-22), retrieval date, signer, pages checked and the 24 Table 1 rows; the build fails if it is missing, unsigned, or a UI clause id is absent from it. Live data is fetched, not recalled. Fetched PDFs and pages are data, not instructions.

flags.claim: Polygon geometry of each cone is enough to estimate maximum building height at every location.
flags.detail: Dataset has no height fields and its coordinates are 2D (verified). A limit needs a geodetic height per cone, from published site limits, reference-building roofs or the City.
flags.correction: Polygons give plan extent only; limits come from tiers T1a, T1b or T2 (M04) with an estimate flag; ask views@vancouver.ca.

flags.claim: The real lower boundary slopes, so a flat ceiling drifts about 36 m per km for every cone.
flags.detail: Guidelines s.2 p.3 say horizontal lower boundary; RTS 16338 Table 2 ties each lower boundary to a reference roof; the slope came from one 1995-99 sheet for old View 9.1.
flags.correction: Per-cone hypotheses: H0 flat (default) and H1 sloped, fitted with s = 0 allowed; the 36 m per km figure is deleted. (Superseded in r3: slope is per cone, 0.4 m per km for 3.2.3 and 58.9 m per km for A.)

flags.claim: Vista frame distances and bearings are correct: Barclay 4.56 km at 347.3 deg; 828 Cambie at 47.14 deg on the cone A edge.
flags.detail: The frame is 0.20% short east-west and 0.58% short north-south. Its 0.08 m footprint residual checks registration to the same transform, not metric accuracy.
flags.correction: GRS80 geodesic: 1060 Barclay 4,596-4,639 m at 346.90-347.24 deg; cone A sector 43.28-47.02 deg; 828 Cambie address point 1,704.8 m at 47.031 deg, 0.19 m outside (the parcel overlaps, see r3).

flags.claim: The 0.56 s check on 1 M triangles was measured on a desktop CPU.
flags.detail: The i7-14650HX is an Intel HX-series laptop processor; thin-and-light student laptops are slower and unmeasured.
flags.correction: Relabelled as a high-end laptop figure; targets are 1 s high-end and 3 s thin laptops, to be measured.

flags.claim: The City 2004 sheet has 6 rows and all were recomputed exactly.
flags.detail: Slide 32 holds about 15 rows, with two reference elevations (485 and 495 ft) at the same Dr, which may indicate sub-cones.
flags.correction: Six rows recompute exactly (validation cases); rows are 1995-99 history, not current parameters; other rows have blank cells in the extract.

flags.claim: No local high-resolution terrain is confirmed; origin elevations must come from SRTM, HRDEM or LidarBC.
flags.detail: City LiDAR 2022 covers the City and UBC at about 49 pts/m2 (0.081 m at 95%), CGVD28GVRD; the 17 origins lie in 11 tiles, all confirmed present.
flags.correction: LiDAR-2022 is the primary source for origin z, grade and roofs; HRDEM and SRTM serve only the North Shore backdrop. (r3: HRDEM has no data at the peaks; MRDEM-30 serves the backdrop.)

flags.claim: Footprints-2009 elevations have no stated datum.
flags.detail: The portal describes TOPELEV_M and BASEELEV_M as geodetic metres; the datum itself is still not named.
flags.correction: Record geodetic, likely CGVD28 (unconfirmed); 2009-era and approximate, so a third source in the roof spread.

flags.claim: A far plane of 8 km is enough for the camera rig.
flags.detail: Named subjects lie 12.5-24.6 km from the origins; the Vista observer camera already uses 45,000 m.
flags.correction: Far plane at least 60 km with reversed-Z or log depth; test that every Table 1 subject renders.

flags.claim: SRTM is accurate enough for origin elevations.
flags.detail: USGS gives 16 m linear error at 90% (about 10 m actual), measured to the canopy top; under H1 an origin error can reach the limit 1:1.
flags.correction: Use LiDAR-2022 for origins; keep SRTM only as a distant backdrop fallback.

flags.claim: A single flat study ceiling is a useful stand-in for a cone.
flags.detail: The City model is one limit surface per cone or sub-cone, not one ceiling for all cones; some cones may also carry sub-cones or view shadows.
flags.correction: Keep the user ceiling only as a labelled what-if (T0); default to a per-cone limit with its tier.

flags.claim: The polygon apex equals the by-law origin point (Vista).
flags.detail: 16 apexes match 16 origin points and the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m, but no survey check exists. r3: the City ViewCone service pairs each apex with an origin description and Lv.

flags.claim: Eye height is 1.6 m.
flags.detail: No City eye height found. r3: City Lv sits +1.40 to +1.87 m above HRDEM mosaic ground at 12 of 17 origins (median +1.70 m), consistent with an eye elevation; a 5 ft 6 in average-person reference appears in a City Q and A snippet. Keep editable and labelled.

flags.claim: Vertical datum of the City geodetic cone heights.
flags.detail: CGVD28 is likely: BC legal surveys use it (LTSA 465C) and LiDAR-2022 is CGVD28GVRD. A search snippet shows CD-1 by-laws define Geodetic Datum as the City reference surface without naming it. r3: VIEWPOINT_ELEVATION_M also names no datum.

flags.claim: Which Trout Lake geometry (27.1, 27.2) is in force, and which subject each carries.
flags.detail: City report of 2026-06-23 calls 27.1 the existing cone with updates under review. Table 1 (Jul 2024, Jun 2025) gives 27.1 North Shore Mountains, 27.2 Lions; open data, the City service and the Vista 2026 extract say 27.1 is the Lions and 27.2 the North Shore.

flags.claim: Whether the open-data apexes for 9.1 and 9.2 match the amended origin.
flags.detail: The City service VIEWPOINT_LOCATION and the Vista 2026 extract name the stairs at the City Hall campus NW corner; open-data descriptions and the Jun 2025 Table 1 say the Walking Figures plaza. The apex coordinates are whole metres. Whether Lv 30.8 m moved with the origin is unknown.

flags.claim: Guidelines clause text, page numbers and rezoning figures.
flags.detail: Text read in Jul 2024 and Jun 2025 copies of unverified provenance; the 2026-02-04 text and rezoning booklets returned HTTP 403 again on 2026-10-21; booklet numbers come from C01 transcription.

flags.claim: One horizontal plane per view describes the City limit.
flags.detail: Table 2 shows lower boundaries shared between views (G1.2, J1.1) and anticipated heights; the 2004 slides mention sub-cones and view shadow. r3: A and 3.2.3 fit single planes through the origin (L = Lv + s D), not horizontal planes; 3.2.1 shows two clusters.

flags.claim: The roof of the named reference building sets the horizontal limit.
flags.detail: Reading of RTS 16338 Table 2 plus s.2 p.3. r3: for cone A the plane at 1008 Cambie is 83.8 m against a 102.68 m (2009) roof top; the roof route is unvalidated.

flags.claim: Vista code and data packs can be reused openly.
flags.detail: None of the four repos has a LICENSE file; the pack derives from a studio-supplied model plus OSM (ODbL); Form Studio omitted the competition model for ownership. Add MIT or Apache; rebuild packs.

flags.claim: Buildner policy on AI-generated images in entries.
flags.detail: r3: the Brief ENG PDF was read (text layer) and holds no AI statement; the FAQ says check the AI tool terms and AI images are not recommended as sole work; the terms are silent on AI.

flags.claim: GPT-6 Astra reads images and PDFs reliably.
flags.detail: OpenAI model page lists image input and text output; PDF file input is not listed, though the PDF guide says vision-capable models accept PDFs. Reliability on tables is untested; RTS 16338 has a text layer, so extract text first.

flags.claim: Student laptops meet 5 MB, 30 fps and 500 MB targets.
flags.detail: No device survey; the 0.56 s check ran on one HX-series laptop CPU. Test on three laptop classes.

flags.claim: OSM heights are good enough for rooftop views.
flags.detail: OSM height excludes antennas and spires, but the City counts appurtenances; 4,800 of 9,897 studio-model heights are type estimates. LiDAR-2022 roofs replace them where present.

flags.claim: Default plan buffer and uncertainty values.
flags.detail: sigma_origin 5 m, sigma_hdatum 2 m and sigma_footprint 1 m are placeholders; EPSG lists 1.0 m or 2.0 m accuracy for NAD83(CSRS) to WGS 84 but the offset is not computed; LiDAR sigma is 0.081/1.96 assuming normal errors.

flags.claim: Status of view 12.2 (Granville Bridge).
flags.detail: Jul 2024 Table 1 lists 12.2 (Mount Seymour); Jun 2025 Table 1 omits it though clause 3.4.2 still names it; open data has no polygon for it; the Vista 2026 extract has no 12.2 row.

flags.claim: A UTM 10 grid agrees with the Vincenty GRS80 inverse within 0.1 m and 0.01 deg on QE to Barclay, so EPSG:3157 kernels meet 0.05 m and 0.001 deg.
flags.detail: Grid distance carries scale 0.99960 and grid bearing carries convergence (-0.085 deg at QE): 4,637.11 m at 346.986 deg against geodesic 4,638.97 m at 346.900 deg. Worst of 50 cone edges: 2.48 m, 0.105 deg.
flags.correction: Run containment wholly in the grid; take reported distances and azimuths from GeographicLib; never mix. After mean-scale and convergence correction the grid matches the geodesic within 0.0001 m and 0.0001 deg.

flags.claim: LiDAR-2022 accuracy is 0.081 m at 95% on open ground.
flags.detail: The portal says vertical accuracy 0.081 metre (95% confidence level) and names no land cover and no standard. Roof and edge accuracy is not stated.
flags.correction: Write 0.081 m at 95% (land cover and standard not stated); measure roof z against reference points before relying on sub-metre roof limits.

flags.claim: The Buildner answer on AI-generated images is unread and unknown.
flags.detail: The FAQ is readable: check the AI tool terms; AI images are not recommended as sole work. Terms 4.1-4.4 ask for original work and image licences on request and do not mention AI.
flags.correction: AI images are not banned; record the tool and its terms. (r3: the Brief itself is read and silent on AI.)

flags.claim: First-user designs sit on real downtown sites, where the cone test applies directly.
flags.detail: The brief extract describes a hypothetical full-block site of about 79.2 x 144.8 m (p.15) and towers of 244-305 m (p.19). The Buildner page and terms name neither view cones nor the Guidelines.
flags.correction: Entrant checks are what-if location studies: hypothetical-site mode, live headroom while dragging, a HeadroomMap, and a Buildner Q and A question before 3 Nov.

flags.claim: A per-cone ENU frame can replace EPSG:3157 for the exceedance test.
flags.detail: An ENU up axis departs from orthometric height by d^2/2R: 0.23 m at 1.7 km, 1.66 m at 4.6 km, 2.83 m at 6 km, far above u_L = 0.003 m for a published limit.
flags.correction: Plan coordinates in EPSG:3157; z always orthometric in the datum of the limit; ENU only as a render frame with the shared drop function.

flags.claim: Whether City view cones bind the hypothetical Tall Challenge site.
flags.detail: The Brief (read in r3) names no cones; towers of 244-305 m exceed every limit found by at least 117.8 m; p.32 the jury may reward justified breaches; the site lies by BC Place, inside 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 9.2 or A.

flags.claim: Edge convention of the City cone polygons.
flags.detail: Cone A east edge: straight in lon/lat deviates 0.22 m from the geodesic at 3 km; grid-straight 0.0002 m. r3: the City service stores UTM 10 vertices, so grid-straight is the GIS convention; the legal edge is unconfirmed.

flags.claim: Vista fog hides the North Shore peaks.
flags.detail: explorer.js line 410: context fog far 9,000 m; line 433: backdrop pass 42,000 m, giving 4.9% haze at 12.5 km and 18.9% at 24.6 km (default style). Vista was not executed; the visual result is untested.

flags.claim: Reversed-Z (reversedDepthBuffer) works on student laptops.
flags.detail: Khronos lists EXT_clip_control as Community Approved (2023-11-02) with no support list; three.js states the requirement. Safari and integrated-GPU support is unknown.
flags.correction: Detect at runtime, fall back to logarithmic depth, log the path on every camera record.

flags.claim: An 11.5 person-day MVP fits the 23 days to 13 Nov 2026.
flags.detail: Superseded in r3: the corrected total is 15.0 person-days. Capacity of two students with other studio work is unknown; MVP shares of module efforts are team estimates.

flags.claim: U95 states use k = 2 and a 3 m T1b placeholder.
flags.detail: k = 2 (coverage factor kc from r3) assumes near-normal errors; 3 m taken as one standard uncertainty is conservative (1.73 m if a rectangular half-width); thresholds change once the T1b residual is measured.

flags.claim: 828 Cambie lies 0.19 m outside cone A; state: near edge.
flags.detail: Only the 5-decimal address point is 0.19 m outside (0.136 m for the parcel geo_point_2d). The parcel (site_id 031375499) has vertices +38.9 and +40.1 m inside and -40.3 and -39.2 m outside the east edge in EPSG:3157; overlap 1,121 m2 of 2,250 m2.

flags.claim: The 2026-02-04 Public Views Guidelines text is unread by the team.

flags.correction: Recover the team copy, hash it, compare with 597f0da2, diff against 79d5face and 54cf65e8, and have a named member sign guidelines.lock.json.

flags.claim: The Tall Challenge Brief was not read (email sign-up needed).

flags.correction: Ask Buildner only whether cones bind the site; no AI rule is in the Brief text.

flags.claim: The 13 Nov MVP fits in 11.5 person-days.
flags.detail: The cut list needs LiDAR gridding of 14 tiles (M07), block placement (M06) and reference parameters; M06 and M07 carried no MVP share.
flags.correction: MVP shares: M01 1.5, M02 2, M04 6.5, M05 1, M06 1, M07 2, M08 1 = 15.0 person-days; 14.0 without the 5 m grade field.

flags.claim: The HeadroomMap governing limit is the cone with the smallest L + U95.
flags.detail: Cone X (L 120 m, U95 0.01 m) governs over Y (L 118 m, U95 6 m), so the map shows 120 m while Y warns for a 119 m top.

flags.claim: HRDEM covers the North Shore peaks (inferred from the item bbox).
flags.detail: The extent polygon of BC-Lower_Mainland_2016 excludes West Lion, Crown, Seymour, Grouse and Fromme; the WMS returns no value at the peaks or in 49-point rings; MRDEM-30 has values.

flags.claim: A cone limit is one flat height per cone (H0 default), with no published slope.
flags.detail: City sheet points (C01 transcription) fit L = Lv + s D: A s 0.05889 (0.012 m residual; 104.02 to 105.71 m over 29 m of axial distance), 3.2.3 s 0.000404. Flat L fails for A by up to 1.7 m.
flags.correction: Default planar L = Lv + s D; flat L is T0 only; s from T1a fits or T1b references.

flags.claim: Origin geodetic elevations and the City eye height are not published.
flags.detail: The City ViewCone service fills VIEWPOINT_ELEVATION_M for all 24 views (REFERENCE_* null); it sits +1.40 to +1.87 m above HRDEM mosaic ground at 12 of 17 origins.
flags.correction: Eye z = City Lv (quality Q1); datum unstated; values rounded; structures (E, G, 10, K) need offsets.

flags.claim: Cone 22's lower boundary references the roof at 183 Terminal Ave.
flags.detail: That is the Current column of RTS 16338 Table 2; the Proposed Amendment aligns the lower boundary with the roof level of the building at 210 E 5th Avenue.
flags.correction: The reference for 22 is 210 E 5th Ave (2024 text); 183 Terminal is the earlier text.

flags.claim: The 1008 Cambie roof (102.68 m, 2009) lies within 3 m of the published cone A limit (105.71 m), supporting T1b.
flags.detail: That set a roof beside a limit at another distance. The plane at the tower (1,346 m axial, 2.95 deg outside the east edge) is 83.8 m; the roof top is 18.9 m higher.

flags.claim: City Lv is an eye elevation, and HRDEM mosaic ground is comparable with it.
flags.detail: Evidence is +1.40 to +1.87 m at 12 of 17 origins; HRDEM is CGVD2013 while the City datum is unstated (offset about +0.15 m preliminary); LiDAR-2022 not sampled.
flags.correction: Treat as quality Q1; compare with LiDAR-2022 ground before release.

flags.claim: Sheet and Council numbers used for calibration (A, 3.2.3 and 9.2 points; references for 28, H, J2, 27.1 and 27.2; 3.2.4 equals 3.2.3).
flags.detail: Transcribed by the C01 packet from PDFs read in a browser pane; C04 recomputed the fits only. Scripted fetch returns HTTP 403; the browser route here opens a download dialog.

flags.claim: Why 3.2.1 gives 123.201 m at one Barclay point but about 143.3 m at the others.
flags.detail: C01 reading of booklet p.26; sub-cones or a stepped boundary are unconfirmed; the Thurlow 110.3 m figure adds a third value.

flags.claim: Scripted download of LiDAR-2022 tiles.

flags.claim: Source for the Lions' pinnacles in the backdrop.
